name: Confirm the data hub of record for the stack
text_content:
Type: founder decision

Source: Session 3 of the Scaling People translation program, page section 13.1 of the S3 page in the Sŏn Operating System doc 2ky45bmy-17253. Session task 86ajgmhgx.

The white paper (p.21) names a specific tool as "the hub for everything that is not CRM," with the reservation platform as the identity spine beneath it and the loyalty engine above it, and describes the AI layer as reading across that hub. The program's source boundary states the same tool is no longer in use for any purpose. The operating system's metric layer, shift close, feedback loop, alert register, and readiness test all run on whatever holds the hub role. Dominic confirms what currently holds it and whether the white paper's five-layer stack description is current. Until confirmed, no operating-system document names a hub tool.

comment.text: Session 13 adds the daily pool calculation to what runs on the hub and the point-of-sale spine: the day's pool is a function of the day's sales record, which is the point-of-sale spine's, and the record names that spine as an open decision; the daily distribution is a function of the schedule, the sheets, the fluency record, and the mentored-plan state, which live on the hub. Until both are confirmed the calculation is a build on the backbone and the partners' page records it as manual. S13 page, sections 9.6 and 18; I4; finding 19.8.

comment.text: Session 11 names what waits on this: the feedback channel's sync to the leads' review record ("syncs to the execution system," WP p.22), the change-reach record's computation, and the copy of a phone-originated message from the phone's software to the book are each recorded on the partners' page as manual until the hub is confirmed and the mesh carries them. No tool on the S11 page is named as the hub, and none becomes one by implication. S11 page, sections 6.8, 6.9, 7.1; P13, P15.
